question: In the channelized-intersection example in Figure 2A-3, how far from the nose of the island is the YIELD sign shown?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Drawing B (channelized intersection) of Figure 2A-3, the sign placed on the channelizing island is dimensioned "2 ft MIN." from the nose of the island (and 2 ft MIN. from the side edge of the island). This matches the general MUTCD recommendation that signs on raised islands maintain at least a 2-foot clearance from the outer edge of the island; the companion YIELD sign along the channelized turn roadway is shown with the standard 6 ft to 12 ft MIN. lateral offset. Guidance (recommended): - "Any signs or signals placed on a raised island in the center of an undivided highway should be installed with a clearance of at least 2 feet from the outer edge of the raised island to the nearest edge of the sign or signal, except as permitted in Section 2A.16." Visual evidence: - [Image 4] Figure 2A-3, Drawing B ("Channelized intersection") shows the sign on the channelizing island dimensioned "2 ft MIN." from the island nose and "2 ft MIN." from the island's side edge, with the YIELD sign for the channelized turn shown at a "6 ft to 12 ft MIN." lateral offset from the pavement edge. - [Image 7] The full-page view of Figure 2A-3 (p.52) confirms the same "2 ft MIN." dimensions at the island nose and side in Drawing B, along with the note that lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. Citations: - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Section 8A.06 Guidance §3 (p.989)
gold_answer: At least 2 feet from the nose of the island.
